## PCA removing the genes that don't move

### Load packages

```{r}
#Load packages 
library(tidyverse)   
library(limma)       # differential expression for microarray data (Bioconductor)
options(bitmapType = "cairo")
library(conflicted)
conflicts_prefer(dplyr::select, dplyr::filter, dplyr::slice, dplyr::lag) #choose which library is default
```

### Separate data

```{r}
dat_avg <- readRDS("../data/data_aug.rds") #read data from the file
dat_avg_wide <- dat_avg |>   #initiate pipeline to make the data wide
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(title,geo_accession, mouse, timepoint, tissue),
              names_from  = ENTREZ_ID,
              values_from = expression
              ) #make the data wide choosing the names of the columns from the entrezID and the expression values while keeping the identification columns


meta <- dat_avg_wide |> #seperatee metadata from experimental data
  dplyr::select(title, geo_accession, mouse, timepoint, tissue) |>
    mutate(
    time   = as.numeric(as.character(timepoint)), #ensure time is saved as numeric
    tissue = as.character(tissue) #ensure tissue is saved as character
  ) 

```

```{r}
expr_mat <- dat_avg_wide |> #seperate experimental data from metadata
  select(-geo_accession, -mouse, -timepoint, -tissue) |>  #remove these columns
  column_to_rownames("title") |>  #make row names the "title" column                    
  as.matrix()   #saved as matrix for prcomp to work

#this chunk makes a table with one sample per row and one gene per column
```

```{r}
#This chunk removes any genes that don't have any variance across all samples and serves no purpose for the PCA analysis, prcomp can't scale a constant column

genes_vary <- expr_mat |>
  as_tibble() |> 
  map_lgl(~ var(.x) > 0) #Mark TRUE each gene with variance >0
expr_mat <- expr_mat[, genes_vary] #Keep all rows and only keep genes marked as true

cat("Samples:", nrow(expr_mat), " Genes:", ncol(expr_mat), "\n")
cat("Genes removed:", sum(!genes_vary))

tissues <- unique(meta$tissue) #make an array of the 5 tissues for the rest of the code
```

Quality Check

```{r}
# Sample-vs-sample distance = 1 - Pearson correlation (the paper's setting).
sample_dist <- as.dist(1 - cor(t(expr_mat)))                   
hc <- hclust(sample_dist, method = "complete")                 
 
# Colour code: one colour per organ (named vector so we can look colours up by organ)
tissue_cols <- set_names(rainbow(length(tissues)), tissues)    # rainbow(5) gives 5 colours; set_names() labels each with its organ

plot(hc, labels = FALSE, hang = -1,                            
     main = "Sample clustering")  
points(seq_along(hc$order), rep(0, length(hc$order)),          
       col = tissue_cols[meta$tissue[hc$order]], pch = 15)    
legend("topright", legend = names(tissue_cols), col = tissue_cols, pch = 15)  
```

### Find only genes that change with fasting

```{r}
#Use limma to find only genes that change significantly with fasting in any tissue

expr_genes_by_samples <- t(expr_mat) #limma needs samples in columns

de_list <- tissues |> #start from vector of tissue names
  set_names() |>                         # name each list element by its organ
  map(function(tis) {                   # map() used to run a function once per organ (list  element)

    keep   <- meta$tissue == tis        # Mark as TRUE samples from current organ
    tfac   <- factor(meta$time[keep])    # organ's timepoints as categories
    design <- model.matrix(~ tfac)       # design table with 0h as baseline and one column for each other timepoint
    
    fit <- lmFit(expr_genes_by_samples[, keep], design) #create a linear model for each gene in the current organ
    fit <- eBayes(fit)                #find p-values of the linear models

    # coef = 2:ncol(design) test if there is any difference from 0h at each timepoint
    # p.value = 0.05 keeps genes with p < 0.05 (difference)
    topTable(fit, coef = 2:ncol(design), number = Inf, p.value = 0.05) |>
      rownames_to_column("gene") |>               # make gene names a column
      pull(gene)                                  # return gene names
  })

# Number of diffretly expressed genes per organ
de_counts <- de_list |>
  map_int(length) |>                              # length of each organ's gene list
  enframe(name = "tissue", value = "n_DE_genes")   # make named vector into a tidy table
print(de_counts)

# Find all genes that change in atleast one organ
de_union <- de_list |> unlist() |> unique()
cat("Total differentyl expressed genes in any tissue:", length(de_union), "\n")

# Expression matrix of only those genes 
expr_de <- expr_mat[, de_union]

# NOTE FOR YOUR METHODS: selecting genes by time and then looking at time
# separation is slightly circular. It is fine for visualising and ranking,
# but state it. The paper's benchmark: brain 45, intestine 656, kidney 1252,
# liver 2068, muscle 3057 DE genes.


```

### Global PCA on DE genes

```{r}
# PCA for all organs
pca <- prcomp(expr_de, scale. = TRUE)

# Variance explained by each PC
var_tbl <- tibble(                                      #make a table with the PCA data
  PC      = seq_along(pca$sdev),                        # PC number 1, 2, 3, ...
  var_pct = pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2) * 100,         # % variance per PC
  cum_pct = cumsum(var_pct)                             # running total (sum of PCs)
)

# Scree plot: how much each of the first 15 PCs explains
var_tbl |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(PC, var_pct)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Principal component", y = "% variance", title = "Scree plot") +
  theme_bw()

#Use smallest number of PCs to explain >=70% of variance, max 10
n_pcs <- var_tbl |>
  filter(cum_pct >= 70) |>      # PCs until their running total has reached 70%
  slice_head(n = 1) |>          # First PC # where running total has reached 70%
  pull(PC)                  # take PC number 
cat("Using", n_pcs, "PCs (", round(var_tbl$cum_pct[n_pcs], 1), "% of variance )\n")

# Scores = coordinates of every sample in PC space, joined with its labels
pc_cols <- paste0("PC", 1:n_pcs) #PCs until reached 70%
scores <- pca$x |> # Coordinate of each sample in each PC
  as_tibble(rownames = "sample") |>
  select(sample, all_of(pc_cols)) |>             
  left_join(meta |> select(title, tissue, time), by = c("sample" = "title")) 

# PC1 vs PC2 plot: colour = organ, shape = time
scores |>
  ggplot(aes(PC1, PC2, color = tissue, shape = factor(time))) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(x = paste0("PC1 - ", round(var_tbl$var_pct[1], 1), "%"),
       y = paste0("PC2 - ", round(var_tbl$var_pct[2], 1), "%"),
       shape = "time (h)", title = "Global PCA (DE genes)") +
  theme_bw()


```

### Euclidean distances

How much each organ's gene expression moves from the 0h centroid at each timepoint

```{r}
# Centroid = the average position of a group of samples (mean of each PC).
centroids <- scores |>
  group_by(tissue, time) |>                      # one group for each organ and timepoint
  summarise(across(all_of(pc_cols), mean), .groups = "drop")  # average each PC within the group and then remove the groups

dist_df <- centroids |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(pc_cols), names_to = "PC", values_to = "value") |>  # one row per organ x time x PC
  group_by(tissue, PC) |> # group per tissue and PC centroid
  mutate(shift = value - value[time == 0]) |> # difference from this organ's 0h value on each PC
  group_by(tissue, time) |>
  summarise(dist = sqrt(sum(shift^2)),  # Euclidean distance = sqrt of summed squared shifts
            .groups = "drop") |>
  filter(time > 0)                         # the 0h-to-0h distance is 0 by definition
print(dist_df)
 
# Plot distance over time
dist_df |>
  ggplot(aes(time, dist, color = tissue)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(12, 24, 48, 72)) +
  labs(x = "Time of fasting (h)",
       y = "Euclidean distance from 0h centroid (PC space)",
       title = "How far has each organ moved from its fed state?") +
  theme_bw()
```
